title: Which Shelter Can Everyone Reach?
locale: 山口県公立高校入試型
sentences: After heavy rain, our town reviewed its emergency shelters and asked students to explain how different residents could reach safe places.
Three buildings appeared on the official list, but the shortest walking route was not necessarily the safest choice for everyone.
The community hall was five minutes away and could hold forty people, but its route crossed the East Bridge.
The elementary school was nine minutes away and had space for eighty, including an entrance without stairs.
The hill gym was fifteen minutes away and could hold sixty residents, although the road to it had a steep section.
At first, Ken recommended the hall because it was nearest and had a large room with tables and chairs.
Mina checked the river warning map and noticed that East Bridge closed whenever the water reached Level Three.
The current notice placed the river at Level Three, so the hall was not reachable by the shortest route shown on our first map.
We then checked a family group of fifty-two people including young children, older residents, and one visitor who used a wheelchair.
Even if East Bridge were open, the hall's forty-person limit would still be too small for that group.
The school had enough capacity and a level entrance, and its route did not cross the bridge marked as closed.
The gym had enough space too, but we wondered whether the steep road would be difficult for everyone to use.
Our teacher reminded us that safety was not a contest to find the smallest travel time and that official instructions came first.
We decided to recommend the school for the group under the conditions shown, while reminding residents to follow current town directions.
Mina added a note to our poster explaining that the river level could change and that yesterday's safe route might close today.
We placed the emergency telephone number beside the route information so families could ask for current guidance.
One resident asked if the gym should be removed from the list completely, because its road was difficult for some people.
Ken replied that the gym might still help others, but its limitations should be shown clearly instead of being hidden from the map.
The town officer thanked us for considering bridge access, capacity, and mobility rather than looking only at distance.
She also checked that our advice did not replace official evacuation orders, which could change as the storm developed.
I learned that useful emergency information must connect numbers to real people's needs and stay open to changes in the situation.
fullTranslation:
大雨の後、町は避難所を見直し、さまざまな住民が安全な場所へ行く方法を生徒に説明するよう求めました。
公式一覧には三つの建物がありましたが、最短の徒歩経路がだれにとっても最も安全とは限りませんでした。
地域会館は徒歩五分で四十人を収容できましたが、行くには東橋を渡る必要がありました。
小学校は徒歩九分で八十人を収容でき、段差のない入口もありました。
丘の体育館は徒歩十五分で六十人を収容できましたが、途中に急な坂がありました。
ケンは最も近く、大きな部屋に机と椅子がある地域会館を最初に勧めました。
ミナは水位がレベル三になると東橋が閉鎖されるという警戒地図の注意書きを見つけました。
その日の川はレベル三だったため、最初の地図にある最短経路では会館に行けませんでした。
次に私たちは、幼い子どもや高齢者、車いす利用者を含む五十二人のグループの条件を考えました。
東橋が開いていたとしても、地域会館の定員四十人では五十二人を収容できませんでした。
小学校には十分な定員と段差のない入口があり、閉鎖された橋を通る必要もありませんでした。
体育館にも定員の余裕はありましたが、急な坂を全員が通れるかは疑問でした。
先生は、安全とは最短時間を競うことではなく、公式の避難指示をまず確認すべきだと話しました。
私たちは示された条件では小学校を勧めることにし、現在の町の指示を必ず確認するよう伝えました。
ミナは水位の変化によって、昨日安全だった道が今日も安全とは限らないと注記しました。
家族が最新の指示を確認できるよう、避難経路の横に緊急連絡先を示しました。
ある住民は急な坂が難しい人もいるので、体育館を一覧から消すべきではないかと質問しました。
ケンは体育館がほかの人には役立つかもしれないので、欠点を隠さず示すべきだと答えました。
町の職員は距離だけでなく、橋の通行状況、定員、移動のしやすさを考慮した点を評価しました。
職員は私たちの案が、気象状況により変わる公式の避難指示の代わりではないことも確認しました。
私は緊急時の情報には、数字と人々の必要を結びつけ、状況の変化に対応する姿勢が必要だと学びました。

materials.title: Shelter options and river warning
materials.note: Current river warning Level 3. Group has 52 members including one wheelchair user. Official evacuation instructions take priority.

questions.prompt: How many people were in the family group?

questions.evidenceJp: 次に私たちは、幼い子どもや高齢者、車いす利用者を含む五十二人のグループの条件を考えました。

questions.prompt: Which shelter holds fifty-two people and avoids the closed bridge with level access?
questions.evidence: The school had enough capacity and a level entrance, and its route did not cross the bridge marked as closed.
questions.evidenceJp: 小学校には十分な定員と段差のない入口があり、閉鎖された橋を通る必要もありませんでした。
questions.reason: 80人定員・段差なし・閉鎖橋回避をすべて満たす。

questions.prompt: Why was the hall's shortest route unavailable?
questions.answer: East Bridge was closed at the current river level.
questions.evidence: The current notice placed the river at Level Three, so the hall was not reachable by the shortest route shown on our first map.
questions.evidenceJp: その日の川はレベル三だったため、最初の地図にある最短経路では会館に行けませんでした。
questions.reason: 現在レベル3で橋が閉鎖されたため。

questions.prompt: Choose the true statement: A the hall held sixty; B the school had stairs at the entrance; C the gym had a steep road; D all routes crossed East Bridge.
questions.evidence: The hill gym was fifteen minutes away and could hold sixty residents, although the road to it had a steep section.
questions.evidenceJp: 丘の体育館は徒歩十五分で六十人を収容できましたが、途中に急な坂がありました。
questions.reason: 体育館への経路には急な坂。

questions.prompt: Why did the teacher say that the shortest journey was not necessarily best?
questions.answer: Safety depended on official warnings, access, and capacity.
questions.evidence: Our teacher reminded us that safety was not a contest to find the smallest travel time and that official instructions came first.
questions.evidenceJp: 先生は、安全とは最短時間を競うことではなく、公式の避難指示をまず確認すべきだと話しました。
questions.reason: 安全には時間以外に制約があるため。

questionSetB.reason: 水位で経路が変わるという注記の直後が自然。

questionSetB.prompt: Complete: Ken said the gym's l________ should be shown clearly.

questionSetB.prompt: How many fewer places did the hall have than the group needed?

questionSetB.prompt: Which is the best summary? A Choose the closest shelter; B Always use the hill gym; C Connect current conditions with varied residents' needs; D Ignore government instructions.
questionSetB.evidence: I learned that useful emergency information must connect numbers to real people's needs and stay open to changes in the situation.
